HARIKA.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117);\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Since it was my starting day I came for the rounds and came to know about the current status of my patients\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EMy unit duty day was on Tuesdays, so in the OP I learned history taking , clinical examination and with the help of our pgs I also learned interpretation of x-rays and ecgs. I also\u0026nbsp; learned\u0026nbsp; what are the investigations should be sent to rule out differential diagnosis and also treatment regimen that should be given for certain diseases.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EWe used to get minimum OP of 80-110 , and I tried to take history of atleast 50-60 patients. It was so interesting for me to see the patients coming with different symptoms for same disease and some times even no symptom.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI learned CNS, CVS, and RESPIRATORY SYSTEM examinations and I also have saved them in my blogs so that they might help me in future.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EDuring the duty days we also looked after the casualty cases which are emergencies and I have also got the opportunity to do CPR for two cardiac arrest patients during my casualty duties but unfortunately they did not survive😢. It was sad but challenging and I would never give up.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EUnder my PGs guidance I got the opportunities to perform pleural tap and ascitic tap.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EPERIPHERAL POSTINGS-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EICU -\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI started my peripheral postings with ICU . These are the most loved duties of mine which really made me much interested in medicine. During my ICU duties I worked under DR. NISHITHA ma'am. With the help of her I learned so much during my duties.My ICU duties helped me to learn monitoring the patients which are so vital in improving their outcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EOn my first ICU duty day two patients went to cardiac arrest one in the morning for which I have done CPR\u0026nbsp; to the patient, it was successful and then the patient was intubated and I have monitored the patient till his discharge and I am also following his health status after the discharge through PaJR group. So I got the opportunity to learn about the patient's condition, the reason for which he was landed and the treatment that has to be given .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EOn the other side the patient with almost similar condition like the first one went in to cardiac arrest in the evening but we couldn't save him although we tried our best. So I realised that there will be different outcomes for different patients and there are many things that should be learnt in every patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EAnd I also came to know why the vitals are really vital for a patient. I learned to monitor the patient with unstable blood pressures on ionotropes and many patients with high blood sugar levels with grbs monitoring and insulin injections.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI also got the opportunity to monitor the ventilator patients. I came to know about\u0026nbsp; CPAP,BiPAP,its working, use and also the patient compliance with it. I felt it was really a great task for me to maintain their complaince with it.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EOverall i learned about the course of the patient in hospital, their outcome and prognosis in ICU duties.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003ENEPHROLOGY -\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EAfter the completion of my ICU duties then I went for my nephrology duties where there I worked under DR. PAVAN KUMAR.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EIn nephrology duties I saw many patients coming for dialysis on shifts per day which really was unexpected for me. Their shooting blood pressure levels surprised me. During dialysis I got the opportunity to make AV FISTULAS, learned about dialysis machine working , advantages and side effects of dialysis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI also got the opportunity to learn from Dr. PAVAN KUMAR sir in performing CENTRAL LINE.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPSYCHIATRY POSTINGS\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI was posted in the department of psychiatry for 15 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EPsychiatry is a subject that I’m very interested in. The mental health is what many people ignore that might lead to disturbance in physical health.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003ESome cases I saw included schizophrenia, panic attacks, depression, bipolar disorder, substance abuse .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI learned history taking from the pgs, learned about many psychiatric illnesses, the questionnaire for a particular psychiatric illness, interpretation, classification and treatment.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EI have seen many patients with substance abuse disorder and many of them joining de-addiction centre.\u0026nbsp; I also have attended few classes given for patients in the deaddiction centre like meditation classes, music therapy, counselling sessions.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EAnd also liked the way to handle the patients with unstable mental health which requires lots of patience and understanding people's mind and counselling them.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EOverall, the general medicine posting was a great learning experience, and taught me important clinical and social skills that will hopefully help be better evaluate and treat patients in the future.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117);
